_readme: Machine-readable register of every official rule figure the public guide publishes.
Each record was re-opened at its source URL on the check date recorded in 'checked'.
A record here verifies LAW, an official benchmark, or an official statistic. It never
verifies a household value, an appraisal, a premium, a bill or a projection.
Values are the official published numbers. Where the guide displays a rounded form
($10 rounding rule), 'display_rounded' records the rounded text that appears on the site
and 'official_exact' keeps the source value so a reader can match the two.
Do not add a record without a source_url that was actually opened and read.

figures.claim: Federal basic exclusion amount for estates of decedents dying in 2026
figures.note: IR-2026-133 (Nov. 5, 2026) confirms $15,000,000 for 2026 and $15,480,000 for 2027. The 'What's new' page attributes the $15,000,000 amount to Public Law 119-21 (signed July 4, 2025).

figures.claim: Federal basic exclusion amount for estates of decedents dying in 2027
figures.note: IR-2026-133, 'Estate Tax Exclusion', states $15,480,000 for 2027 deaths, up from $15,000,000 for 2026.

figures.claim: Form 706 filing test: gross estate plus adjusted taxable gifts plus specific gift tax exemption compared with the filing threshold
figures.note: The IRS page states a filing is required if the gross estate, increased by adjusted taxable gifts and specific gift tax exemption, exceeds the filing threshold for the year of death. Deductions reduce the taxable estate, not the filing test. This distinction is why no household headroom can be published.

figures.claim: No California estate tax return is required for decedents dying on or after 1 January 2005
figures.note: California State Controller: 'For decedents that die on or after January 1, 2005, there is no longer a requirement to file a California Estate Tax Return.' California has no separate inheritance tax for such deaths either; the page says the Inheritance Tax is only collected for decedents who died before June 8, 1982.

figures.claim: California does not impose an inheritance tax on beneficiaries for modern deaths
figures.note: Same Controller page: the Inheritance Tax is collected only for decedents who died prior to June 8, 1982. The federal estate tax, not a state inheritance tax, is the exposure to test.

figures.claim: Basis of inherited property is generally fair market value on the date of death, or the alternate valuation date if the executor elects it on a timely Form 706
figures.note: Alternate valuation requires an estate tax return and an election. Rev. Rul. 2023-2 is the exception example the guide cites for a grantor-trust fact pattern outside the estate.

figures.claim: Exclusion of up to $250,000 of gain on sale of a main home ($500,000 on a qualifying joint return), subject to ownership and use tests
figures.note: Ownership test: owned at least 24 of the last 60 months. Use test: used as residence at least 24 of the previous 60 months. The exclusion is not automatic.

figures.claim: Proposition 19 intergenerational transfer value allowance for transfers 16 Feb 2025 through 15 Feb 2027
figures.note: BOE LTA 2025/009 sets $1,044,586 using the 2.15% FHFA California HPI change for 2024. The site displays the nearest-$10 form, $1,044,590, and labels it as rounded. Prior periods: $1,000,000 (16 Feb 2021 - 15 Feb 2023) and $1,022,600 (16 Feb 2023 - 15 Feb 2025). The next adjustment occurs February 2027 and its amount is unknown.

figures.claim: Family-home relief requires the transferee to occupy the home as a principal residence within one year and to file the homeowners' or disabled veterans' exemption within one year of transfer for exclusion from the transfer date
figures.note: A late exemption claim gives prospective relief only, beginning the year the claim is filed. Renting the home instead of occupying it does not meet the family-home condition.

figures.claim: BOE-19-P claim is due within three years of transfer and before transfer to a third party, and is also timely if filed within six months of the supplemental or escape assessment notice
figures.note: If the exclusion claim is late, relief can still apply but begins the year the claim is filed.

figures.claim: Proposition 13 limits the annual inflation adjustment to a property's factored base year value to no more than 2%, and the assessor enrolls the lower of factored base year value or market value
figures.note: BOE LTA 2025/023 (Pub 800-10 information sheet) also warns that a property in Proposition 8 decline-in-value status can rise more than 2% on a later lien date, though never above its factored base year value.

figures.claim: Official Proposition 13 inflation factor for the 2026-27 assessment year
figures.note: LTA 2026/002 (Jan. 13, 2026) sets the factor at 1.02. California CPI rose 3.307% (Aug 2024 to Aug 2025, substituting for unavailable October data after the fall 2025 federal shutdown); the 2% constitutional cap applies. The same LTA publishes the full 1976-77 to 2026-27 factor history used on the real-conditions page.

figures.claim: Of the 51 published assessment years 1976-77 through 2026-27, the factor reached the full 2% cap in 40 years (78%) and compounded at about 1.81% a year
figures.note: Derived by counting the rows of the enclosed factor table in LTA 2026/002. Factors below 2% occurred in 1983-84 and 1995-96 through 2004-05 in part, and in 2010-11 (negative), 2011-12, 2014-15, 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2021-22. This is a count of official published values, not a forecast.

figures.claim: San Francisco secured property tax rate for fiscal year 2026-27
figures.note: Treasurer & Tax Collector page states the FY 2026-27 secured rate is 1.18162182%. Direct charges and special assessments can be additional. The model holds this rate constant as a scenario; the page does not forecast future rates.

figures.claim: Allowable annual rent increase for covered units, 1 March 2026 through 28 February 2027
figures.note: SF Rent Board report. Applicability depends on the unit being covered and on correct notice. The same page carries the 9 Nov 2026 notice that File 261020 is proposed and not enacted.

figures.claim: Proposed ordinance File 261020 to limit combined banked and capital-improvement increases is not enacted as of the 9 Nov 2026 notice
figures.note: The Rent Board page states: 'This legislation has not been enacted and is subject to change.' The guide therefore treats it as a watchlist item, not current law.

figures.claim: Where an interest in real property is transferred by reason of death, including through a trust, the change in ownership statement must be filed within 150 days after the date of death
figures.note: Revenue and Taxation Code section 480(b) names trust transfers expressly and places the duty on the trustee (if the property was held in trust) or the transferee. Probate estates use the inventory-and-appraisal timing instead.

figures.claim: Trustee notification must be served not later than 60 days following the triggering event, subject to the section's exceptions
figures.note: Probate Code section 16061.7(f). The 60-day period starts later if there is a trustee vacancy. Not every trust triggers the same notice or deadline, so the guide says so.

figures.claim: H.R. 1301 (119th Congress) was introduced 13 Feb 2025 and referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means; it has not been enacted
figures.official_exact: Introduced; referred to Ways and Means
figures.note: Congress.gov shows Latest Action: House - 02/13/2025 Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means, and tracker status 'Introduced'.

figures.claim: SB 284 (2025-2026) remains an active bill in committee and has not been enacted
figures.note: Official status page: 'Active Bill - In Committee Process', last history action 07/14/25 'Set, final hearing. Held in committee and under submission.'

figures.claim: CPI-U rose 6.5% over the 12 months ending December 2022; electricity rose 14.3% over the same period
figures.note: BLS archived release USDL-23-0017, Table A, unadjusted 12-month changes. Used only to show that a single inflation rate can miss wide divergence between categories.

figures.claim: Annual-average CPI-U change from 1991 through 2025: arithmetic mean 2.62%, median 2.63%, standard deviation 1.41%, range -0.36% (2009) to 8.00% (2022); 10 of 34 years above 3%
figures.note: Computed from the annual-average CPIAUCNS series (BLS data via FRED), downloaded 13 Nov 2026, annual averages 1990-2025. The arithmetic is reproducible from the published series; the statistics themselves are a derived summary, not an official BLS statistic. The 2026 year is incomplete and is excluded.

figures.claim: CBO's February 2026 baseline projects PCE inflation returning to roughly 2% in 2030 and stabilizing thereafter, over a 2026-2036 horizon
figures.note: CBO publication 61882, The Budget and Economic Outlook: 2026 to 2036. The horizon ends in 2036. Nothing in it is a 50-year housing or portfolio forecast, and the guide says so.

figures.claim: 72% probability of at least one magnitude 6.7 or greater earthquake somewhere in the San Francisco Bay region between 2014 and 2043
figures.note: USGS Fact Sheet 2016-3020. It is a regional probability, not the probability of loss at a particular parcel, and it does not price damage or insurance.

figures.claim: Freddie Mac PMMS 30-year fixed rate averaged 7.11% as of 12 November 2026
figures.note: Weekly survey average of applications. Recorded as an observed benchmark only. The guide models no mortgage, so this does not enter any projection.

figures.claim: Cupertino water is supplied through three separate systems: California Water Service (northeast), San Jose Water Company (southeast), and the City-owned system operated by San Jose Water Company under lease (west)
figures.note: This is why a ZIP code alone cannot establish a water bill, and why the guide leaves water amounts blank rather than publishing an estimate.

figures.claim: Santa Clara County documentary transfer tax is $0.55 per $500 of value, equivalent to $1.10 per $1,000
figures.official_exact: $0.55 per $500 or fractional portion of real property value
figures.note: VERIFIED 2026-11-13 (was unverified). The County Clerk-Recorder 'Recording real estate' page states the documentary transfer tax is computed at $.55 per $500 or fractional portion of real property value; $1.10 per $1,000 is the exact equivalent. The same page states San Jose, Palo Alto and Mountain View add $1.65 per $500 (R&T Code 11911), so the town add-on varies by city. The guide still does not publish this rate as a table row; sale costs remain a single invented percentage on the synthetic example.

figures.claim: Maximum FDIC deposit insurance coverage for a trust owner with five or more beneficiaries
figures.official_exact: $1,250,000 per owner for all trust accounts at the same bank
figures.note: FDIC 'Your Insured Deposits': as of April 1, 2024 the maximum coverage for a trust owner with five or more beneficiaries is $1,250,000 per owner for all trust accounts (POD/ITF, revocable and irrevocable) held at the same bank. The page also states coverage does not cover investments, even if bought at an insured bank.
